svg.aria-label: Primary succession timeline in four stages, left to right, starting from glacier-scraped bare rock in Yosemite. Pioneer stage, 0 to 150 years: lichen and crevice plants on bare granite and tiny rock bits. Early intermediate, 150 to 500 years: grasses and wildflowers with primary consumers; gravelly, shallow soil. Late intermediate, 500 to 1,000 years: shrubs and small trees with secondary consumers; moderate soil. Climax community, 1,000 plus years: large trees, tertiary consumers and apex predators; deep, rich soil. A soil layer beneath the stages thickens from left to right. Arrows below: light reaching the ground decreases; biodiversity and soil depth increase.
svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Primary succession timeline (Yosemite)
svg.text: Primary succession: from bare rock to a climax community (Yosemite)
